item.title: [6.9] OmniReasoning: Pushing the Limits of Audio-Visual Joint Reasoning
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Recent advances have enabled unified omni-modal models in understanding audio, vision, and language. However, existing benchmarks, training data, and learning methods largely treat the modalities independently, leaving the capability of audio-visual joint reasoning poorly evaluated and insufficiently elicited. We address this gap with a benchmark, data engine, and learning method.

WHY IT MATTERS

This paper addresses a notable gap in multimodal AI by introducing a dedicated benchmark and training data for true audio-visual joint reasoning rather than independent modality processing.

item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Large language models (LLMs) are highly sensitive to the prompts used to specify task objectives and behavioral constraints. Many recent prompt optimization methods iteratively rewrite prompts using LLM-generated feedback, but the resulting prompts often become longer, accumulate narrow sample-specific rules, and generalize poorly beyond the training distribution. WHY IT MATTERS

TextReg offers a principled regularization approach to mitigate prompt distributional overfitting, moving beyond heuristic prompt optimization methods.

item.title: [6.7] Global Market: BOJ seen nearing 2% inflation target as markets eye December rate hike
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

The Bank of Japan may signal later this month that underlying inflation has reached its 2% target, strengthening expectations for a December rate hike. While policymakers remain cautious after recent increases, steady wages, rising prices and yen weakness could support further tightening as the BOJ gradually normalises monetary policy.

WHY IT MATTERS

Potential shift in BOJ monetary policy toward a December rate hike impacts global carry trades and currency markets, making it relevant for macroeconomic positioning.
